content.glance: s. 96 first appeal. s. 100 second appeal. s. 104 / Order XLIII orders. s. 114 review. s. 115 revision.
content.study:
Introduction
Choose the correct doorway. First appeal (s. 96) is on facts and law from an original decree. Second appeal (s. 100) is only on a substantial question of law. Appeals from orders follow s. 104 and Order XLIII. Review (s. 114 / Order XLVII) is by the same court on a narrow ground. Revision (s. 115) watches jurisdiction where no appeal lies.

Illustration
Trial court decrees after evidence. First appeal under s. 96 can re-appreciate facts.

Fail-illustration
Loser wants the High Court in second appeal to say the trial court believed the wrong witness. That is not a substantial question of law.

Authority
Banarsi v. Ram Phal (2003) 1 SCC 727 — first appeal is the last court of fact.
Santosh Hazari (2001) 3 SCC 179 — substantial question of law.
S.S. Khanna AIR 1964 SC 497 — revision is jurisdictional.
BCCI v. Netaji Cricket Club (2005) 4 SCC 741 — review is not an appeal in disguise.

Close with ss. 96, 100, 114 and 115 CPC, 1908.

rows.right: Review: same court. Revision: High Court

rows.left: s. 96 facts+law; s. 100 only substantial law

cases.name: Banarsi v. Ram Phal
cases.holding: First appellate court must weigh the evidence.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Distinguish first appeal and second appeal.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: s. 96: original decree; facts and law; not from a consent decree. s. 100: appellate decree; substantial question of law must be formulated. Banarsi; Santosh Hazari. Cite ss. 96 and 100 CPC, 1908.

questionsAndAnswers.question: High Court in second appeal re-appreciates oral evidence and reverses. Discuss.
questionsAndAnswers.answer:
Issue. Is that permitted?
Rule. s. 100 — substantial question of law only. Kondiba Kadam (1999) 3 SCC 722.
Application. Re-trying witnesses is a first-appeal function.
Conclusion. The second appeal is unsustainable unless a legal question was first framed.
